data.text/markdown:
Tori Trades · the top-down lines at one moment, one line per chart

Pick a stock, a date and a time of day. For each side the notebook draws one line per chart, top-down, as you described it (2026-10-27): one upward line (for longs) and one downward line (for shorts) each on the daily, the 4-hour, the 1-hour and the 15-minute chart (topdown.cascade). Section 3 then trades these lines over the stock's whole history.
  1. Daily. The line starts at the extreme of the daily candles in view: the lowest low for the upward line, the highest high for the downward one.
  2. 4-hour, 1-hour, 15-minute. Each line starts at the point B of the line above it, moved onto this chart's candle that holds the same price.
  3. Every line is the steepest ray from its point A that no candle of its chart crosses. The candle that stops it fixes its angle, and that candle is point B.
  4. Noise bands (optional). The stock's noise is the moving average of its candles' true range, on each chart and recomputed at every candle. With bands on, a line is a band of line band × noise: a candle may reach into it without stopping the line, and point B is the latest candle inside it. Around the traded 15-minute line, the price's own price band widens it into a contact zone. A touch reaches into the zone, a break closes beyond it, and the stop sits beyond it.
  5. Not a line yet. A line whose angle candle is still among the newest confirm candles is a pending ray, and so is a line shorter than its chart's minimum. The charts below a pending ray draw nothing.
  6. The setup. A side trades only when its 15-minute line exists. Section 1 names that line, or says where the chain stopped.
Every chart is cut at the chosen moment, exactly as the trade replay (bounce.py) cuts it. The last candle of a higher chart may still be forming: at 11:00 today's daily candle holds only the first hour and a half. Every knob sits in the settings below, one per row.

Settings

The stock

Any ticker with daily and 1-minute candles in the database.

The moment (sections 1 and 2)

The session whose lines you want to see.
New York time: the lines see only the candles before it.
Sessions after the moment, drawn faded: the lines never see them.

The lines (every section)

The daily line starts at the extreme (lowest low, highest high) of these daily candles.
Candles that must follow a line's angle candle before the line counts.
Daily candles a daily line needs between its points A and B.
4-hour candles a 4-hour line needs between its points A and B.
1-hour candles a 1-hour line needs between its points A and B (4 = 4 hours).
15-minute candles a 15-minute line needs between A and B (16 = 4 hours).
The first 15-minute candles of every session neither stop the 15-minute line nor become its point B (shown faded).
The same for the last 15-minute candles of every session.

Noise bands (every section)

Draw every line as a band and trade a contact zone, both sized by the stock's noise. Off: exact lines.
Candles in the moving average of the true range: the noise, on each chart, recomputed at every candle.
Half-width of a line's band, in noise of its chart: a candle may reach into it without stopping the line, and point B is the latest candle inside it.
The price's own uncertainty, in 15-minute noise: with the line band it makes the contact zone around the traded line.

The trade (section 3)

Next open: a candle comes to the line and closes on its side, in at the next open. Limit: an order rests at the line plus the entry gap.
How close (in typical candles) a low (high) must come to the line to be a signal. With noise bands the contact zone sets it instead.
The stop starts this many typical candles beyond the line (beyond the contact zone with noise bands) and follows each new swing.
Take the profit at this many R (R = the entry's distance to the first stop). 0: no target, her rule.
Candles after the bounce that must close on the line's side before the entry (next-open entries). A close beyond the line among them: no trade.
After a break, keep the new pending 15-minute line: it trades once its angle candle is confirmed, without waiting for the session's close.
No position is opened or closed on the first 15-minute candles of a session.
The same for the last 15-minute candles of a session.
The most profitable trades of each side drawn in section 3.
Trades the whole 1-minute history; a first run takes a minute or so, the same settings are then read from disk.

NOW, last 15-minute close 158.98; a typical 15-minute candle is 0.67 (the median range of the last 150). Noise bands on: the 15-minute noise is 0.67 now (the average true range of the last 10 candles). Each line's band is ±0.25 × its chart's noise (±0.17 on the 15-minute chart now), and the contact zone ±0.5 × the 15-minute noise (±0.33). Long (upward lines): no 15-minute line, no trade: the chain stops at the 15-minute chart, whose line is not a line yet (its angle candle is still too new, or it is shorter than that chart's minimum).
Short (downward lines): no 15-minute line, no trade: no daily line: the highest high of the 150 daily candles in view is one of the newest 2 (price is at its 150-session high), so no downward line can start yet. Pick an earlier date, or show more daily candles. Each side's lines, top-down (each point B is the next line's point A):

2 · Chart by chart

Each chart shows its own line and the lines of the charts above it, with their noise bands when those are on. The daily chart shows its candles in view; every lower chart starts a little before the point A of its own line, so both anchors are in view. Hover over a line or an anchor for its points. The dotted vertical line is the moment chosen.

data.text/markdown:
3 · Walk forward: trading these lines

The replay (bounce.replay with method="cascade") walks the stock's whole 1-minute history candle by candle, from the session after its first 1-minute one. It draws these same lines (one per chart and side, with the settings above) using only what was known at each moment. It trades the 15-minute line: a side with none does not trade. Long and short are replayed separately, so a short never blocks a long, and the other way round. When the lines are drawn again (never after every candle):
  • While waiting: when a candle breaks the 15-minute line without giving a signal (it closes beyond the line, or beyond the contact zone with noise bands), and at every session's close.
  • In a trade: never. The trade keeps its line until it ends, and the lines are drawn again right after.
  • After a break: the new 15-minute line is usually still pending, because the candle that broke the old one is its angle candle. With watch on it is kept, and it trades once confirm candles have followed its angle candle.
The trade:
  • In: a candle comes to the line and closes on its side, in at the next open; or a limit order resting at the line plus the entry gap.
  • Bounce confirmation: the next N candles must not close beyond the line.
  • Stop: it starts the stop room beyond the line, and follows each new swing.
  • Out: the stop, a close beyond the line (out at the next open), or the profit target.
  • Session edges: no position is opened or closed on the left-out candles.
  • Noise bands: with them on, "the line" is the contact zone. A touch reaches into it, a break and an exit close beyond it, and the stop sits beyond it. A close inside it, beyond the line, is noise: neither a signal nor a break.
  • Money: the whole $10,000 wallet in every trade, at the repo's costs.
Press walk forward in the settings.
